labs.title: Lab 1: Client Network Preflight & Assessment Map (Zero Spend)
labs.objective: Understand AVD required endpoints, client-side latency/jitter, and how avd-assess maps every control plane before deploying anything.
steps: Open https://avd-ops.app/ (or avd-linecheck) from your local machine and run a network check—note RTT, jitter, and endpoint reachability.
In avd-assess, inspect pillars.yaml and dimensions.yaml to see how networking-client and networking-azure map to Microsoft Learn pins.
Compare your local network test against the RDP Shortpath / Reverse Connect requirements in avd-assess/methods/network.md.
verify: You can explain why TCP 443 Reverse Connect succeeds even when UDP Shortpath is blocked.
You can locate the exact dimension row in avd-assess/dimensions.yaml for enableAvdPrivateLink.
labs.gapCheck: Did any endpoint in avd-linecheck or avd-assess lack a clear explanation for an AZ-140 learner? Log it as a gap in avd-assess or avd-linecheck.

labs.title: Lab 2: Read-Only Discovery & Redacted C11 Facts
labs.objective: Run avd-current-state read-only in Azure Cloud Shell to inspect what is deployed across all five control planes and validate the redacted C11 output.
steps: Open Azure Cloud Shell (PowerShell) in a throwaway lab subscription.
Run the avd-current-state single-block collector from its quick start (read-only; makes zero changes).
Inspect the generated redacted C11 JSON and verify that no tenant IDs, subscription IDs, or user names appear.
Cross-reference two C11 findings against avd-assess/methods/scoring.md.
verify: C11 output passes avd-current-state schema validation.
You can trace a C11 fact back to its plane (azure, entra, intune, m365, or power-platform).
labs.gapCheck: Did avd-current-state miss an AZ-104/AZ-140 setting you expected to see, or was a C11 field unclear? Record it as a gap for avd-current-state.

labs.title: Lab 3: Target-State Baseline Design (C14 Manifest, Zero Spend)
labs.objective: Turn C11 facts + workload intake into a C14 target-state manifest for a single pooled host pool.
steps: Open the avd-migrate portal (https://avd-ops.app/migrate/) or CLI.
Configure a pooled Windows 11 Multi-session host pool: pick VM SKU, maxSessionLimit, FSLogix Premium_LRS quota, and Entra ID join.
Export the C14 manifest and compare its workload tier assumptions against avd-second-brain/knowledge/rules/workload-tiers.json.
verify: You have a valid, redacted C14 target-state manifest.
You can justify your maxSessionLimit and profileShareQuotaGiB choices for an AZ-140 design question.
labs.gapCheck: Were any AZ-140 parameters (e.g., scaling plan, RDP properties, Private Link) missing or hard to understand in avd-migrate? Log it.

labs.title: Lab 4: Deploy & Tear Down an AVD Landing Zone in a Throwaway Lab
labs.costEstimate: Paid Azure resources (~$1-3 for a short 1-2 hour lab session; tear down immediately after)
labs.objective: Deploy a minimal AVD landing zone with avd-landing-zone, validate it with avd-current-state, connect a test session, and tear it down cleanly with zero lingering meter.
steps: Use a dedicated throwaway lab subscription. Generate your deployment parameters in https://avd-ops.app/deploy/ (or avd-landing-zone).
Paste the Cloud Shell deployment block to provision the host pool, workspace, VNet, and FSLogix storage.
Sign in via the Windows App / Web Client to verify the session and FSLogix VHDX mount.
Run avd-current-state against the deployed lab to confirm green validation.
Run the teardown script immediately when finished, keeping teardown logs (-TeardownLogs Keep) and verifying zero running VMs/meters remain.
verify: Session host registered as Available in the host pool.
FSLogix profile VHDX created in the Azure Files share.
Teardown completed with zero billing VMs left behind.
labs.gapCheck: Did any Bicep parameter, RBAC role, or teardown step fail or confuse you? Open an issue/note in avd-landing-zone.
